# ethereum-optimism/optimism Weekly Report (Jun 21 - 27, 2026)

## 🚀 Highlights
This week focused heavily on the integration of experimental zkVM-based fault proofs and the continued decoupling of the monorepo from `op-geth`. A major milestone was reached with the integration of **kona-sp1**, bringing SP1-based fault proof capabilities for OP Stack state transitions into the monorepo. Significant effort was also directed toward stabilizing the Superchain ecosystem through `op-reth` enhancements, consensus surface hardening for the Superchain Dependency Manager (SDM), and a comprehensive update of the Go toolchain to version 1.26.4.

## 🛠️ Key Developments

### zkVM and Fault Proof Integration
The project made significant strides in zero-knowledge infrastructure and dispute game mechanics.
*   **Kona-SP1 Integration:** Integrated `kona-sp1` into the monorepo, providing an experimental zkVM-based fault proof system ([#21489](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21489)). This included adding a range-executor and SP1 execution action tests ([#21528](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21528)).
*   **Dispute Game Refinements:** Renamed the `SUPER_PERMISSIONED_CANNON` game type to `SUPER_PERMISSIONED` to reflect its broader applicability ([#21513](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21513)).
*   **Kona Protocol Updates:** Bumped `brotli-decompressor` to v5.0.1 to resolve decompression issues ([#21505](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21505)) and added support for extended transaction envelopes in `L2BlockInfo` ([#21503](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21503)).

### `op-reth` and Execution Layer Enhancements
Work continued on making `op-reth` a first-class execution client for the OP Stack.
*   **Sequencer Support:** Enabled `op-devstack` to support `op-reth-premium` as a drop-in sequencer for acceptance tests ([#21515](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21515)).
*   **Transaction Validation:** Fixed a critical bug in `op-reth` where invalid interop transactions were not being correctly evicted during revalidation ([#21447](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21447)).
*   **Feature Modularization:** Made `chainspec reth-codec` an opt-in feature ([#21483](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21483)) and made the `OpPoolBuilder` ordering injectable ([#21531](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21531)).

### Protocol Stability and Decoupling
The "op-geth decoupling" initiative saw major progress, reducing dependencies on the legacy Geth codebase.
*   **Superchain Package Migration:** Decoupled the monorepo from `op-geth`'s superchain package, establishing `op-core/superchain` as the primary package ([#21487](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21487)).
*   **Core Wiring:** Wired `op-node` onto `op-core/eip1559` and `op-service/txinclude` onto `op-core/fees` ([#21508](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21508)).
*   **Consensus Hardening:** Stabilized the PostExec consensus surface with a `0x7D` guard and TOCTOU mechanisms ([#21502](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21502)).
*   **Karst Upgrade Fix:** Corrected the Karst upgrade gas application to ensure it only applies to the activation block ([#21441](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21441)).

### Infrastructure and Tooling
*   **Toolchain Update:** Updated the global Go toolchain to `1.26.4` across all images and configurations ([#21452](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21452)).
*   **CI Reliability:** Addressed flaky fuzz tests by preventing CPU oversubscription ([#21517](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21517)) and implemented retry mechanisms for network fetches in Docker builds ([#21478](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21478)).

## 🐛 Issues & Triage

### Closed Issues
*   **Interoperability:** Completed the renaming of `interop_time` to `lagoon_time` across the registry and dependent packages ([#21135](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/21135)).
*   **Dispute Games:** Successfully dropped feature flags for v2 dispute game contracts and stopped the deployment of legacy blueprints ([#17262](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/17262)).
*   **Kona Integration:** Finalized the migration of `op-succinct` changes into Kona and updated to the latest SP1 version ([#18457](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/18457)).

### New & Active Issues
*   **Sync Mode Consolidation:** A new proposal aims to merge `syncmode=CL` and `syncmode=EL` into a single mode to simplify node operations ([#21506](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/21506)).
*   **`op-challenger` Permissioned Games:** Ongoing discussion regarding the requirement for `cannon-prestate` in permissioned games, with maintainers looking to simplify the migration path to permissionless games ([#21470](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/21470)).
*   **Performance Optimization:** Investigation is underway regarding potentially redundant `eth_getProof` calls in `kona-host` ([#21510](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/21510)).

## 💬 Community & Collaboration
The week was characterized by high-velocity internal refactoring and cross-component coordination. The "op-geth decoupling" effort shows tight collaboration between protocol engineers to move core logic into `op-core`. Documentation saw a significant refresh, with multiple PRs consolidated to ensure release notes for `kona`, `proxyd`, and the general monorepo are synchronized with the latest GitHub tags. The rapid integration of `kona-sp1` suggests a strong push toward diversifying the fault-proof ecosystem with ZK technology.
